newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebels blamed as Colombia bomb kills at least four.
newsitem.headline: Rebels blamed as Colombia bomb kills at least four.

text.p: Suspected leftist guerrillas detonated a powerful bomb that killed at least four people and seriously injured more than 40 others as it ripped through a building in Medellin on Wednesday, police said.

Gen. Luis Ernesto Gilibert, deputy director of the National Police, blamed the attack on Marxist rebels and suggested they were targeting the offices of a local businessman who runs one of the government-backed civilian self-defence groups known as Convivirs.
Rebels and human rights organisations say such groups are right-wing paramilitary squads.

The explosion in the downtown area occurred at about 11:20 a.m. (1620 GMT) and was caused by a remote-controlled bomb made of about 155 pounds (70 kg) of dynamite, Gilibert said. The device was planted under a stairway in the building, which houses a popular eatery and a civic group known as Asocomunal headed by John Jairo Castano, the leader of a local Convivir.

"Castano is head of a Convivir and chairman of Asocomunal. That would appear to give us an indication of who is behind this attack ... It's clear that this person seems to have been the target of the guerrilla," Gilibert told reporters.
Police said three men and one woman were killed. Rescue workers at the scene told local media other victims could be trapped under the rubble of the building.
The blast occurred a short distance from one of Medellin's largest companies, Empresas Publicas de Medellin, and its president, Mauricio Restrepo, called it "extremely powerful."
"The shock wave moved us all off our seats," he added.
In an interview with the Radionet radio news network, Castano accused a local government official of organising the attack in league with Medellin's guerrilla militias.

"This problem stems from last month, when the community development secretary blamed us for creating a law and order problem. I believe he met with the militias and provided them with the necessary material in return for dislodging us from the building," he said.

Newly appointed Defence Minister Alberto Gonzalez condemned the attack. "This is a barbaric act which has plunged humble households into mourning. We will hunt down those who are staining our streets with blood," he said.

Medellin, which has Colombia's worst violent crime, is often described as the murder capital of the world. Gunmen of the left and right have killed with impunity for years and it was a hotbed of bomb attacks and political assassinations in the late 1980s and early 1990s, when authorities were waging war with the now defunct Medellin drug cartel.
